inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Tanshin consolidated cash-flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expenses' add-back (equity-settled stock acquisition rights). Equity-award taxes are nil (no net-share settlement withholding under J-GAAP). The cash-settled 'virtual stock option' plan is expensed through opex and provisions and is therefore already inside EBITDA; it is not in this line.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity purchase of treasury stock JPY 10,000m (FY2024: 40,000m; H1 FY2026: 4,999m). The company is a repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 140,901,604 issued less 11,109,268 treasury = 129,792,336 at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 FY2026 Tanshin cover), plus 769,302 dilutive stock acquisition rights from the FY2025 diluted-EPS table = 130.56m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.fx_note: Reporting and quote currency are both JPY; no conversion. Roughly two-thirds of revenue and a majority of costs are in USD/EUR/other, so the JPY flows carry translation exposure; management's FY2026 forecast assumes USD 156 / EUR 183. That exposure is charged in the scenario flows, not in the discount rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close 15:30 JST, Friday 30-Oct-2026; valuation date is a Saturday so this is the latest close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows: 10-year JGB ~1.5-2.0% risk-free, ~5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.0-1.1 for a mid-cap, all-equity security-software name gives a cost of equity of ~7.3-8.0%; rounded to 8.0%. No interest-bearing debt, so WACC equals the cost of equity. Not stacked with any ad-hoc premium: single-business concentration, AI-cost margin risk and FX translation are all priced in the probability-weighted scenario flows, and the same 8.0% is used in every scenario so risk is charged exactly once.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed in opex and there are no lease liabilities on the balance sheet (no interest-bearing debt at all; the Tanshin prints the debt-redemption ratio as '-'). No IFRS-16 adjustment is needed; nothing deducted from flows and nothing added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: non-controlling interests of JPY 498m at FY2025 year-end with a JPY -423m share of income. Not deducted; FY0 NOPAT ties to attributable net income within non-operating noise (FX loss JPY 6,224m and a JPY 1,488m retirement-benefit extraordinary loss in FY2025).
inputs.net_cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents JPY 214,195m at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 FY2026 Tanshin, consolidated cash-flow statement) with zero interest-bearing debt. Marketable securities of JPY 11,461m at the same date go in equity_bridge as the matching asset for the stripped interest/investment income. Deferred revenue of JPY 232,485m is an operating liability (prepaid subscriptions): the cost of serving it sits in the projected margins and the ongoing float in wc_capture, so it is not netted against cash. Equity-method affiliates (JPY 1,046m loss share in FY2025) are ignored.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1, operating software company), with the non-US adaptations applied: JPY-built WACC, J-GAAP lease treatment (none needed), matching-asset rule for the securities portfolio. FY0 is FY2025 (calendar year to 31-Dec-2025); year 1 is FY2026, now ten months elapsed, so the year-1 drivers are set to the August 2026 revised guidance (sales JPY 301.5bn, operating income JPY 44.4bn) rather than the February plan or FY2025's peak 20.9% operating margin. Owner FCF = reported FCF 41,780 - SBC 1,410 - interest income 3,527 = 36,843 (13.3% of revenue); interest income is stripped because net cash is ~5.8x the FCF base. Reported EBITDA in the Metrics CSV is after the SBC expense, so ebitda_margin_path is stated pre-SBC (FY2025: 84,834 + 1,410 = 86,244, 31.2%). Component build: EBITDA less SBC less D&A gives EBIT, which ties to FY2026 guided operating income in year 1 (24.2% x 301,370 - 0.5% - 9.0% = ~44,300). The share price is near its 52-week high despite the August cut, having recovered from the January low; the quote therefore already discounts a margin recovery (or renewed take-private interest), and the valuation does not add a takeover premium. Price is a regular TSE close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 Tanshin balance sheet; the matching asset for the stripped interest/investment income (section 7d).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Revenue 3-year CAGR (7.2%) adjusted for yen depreciation over FY2022-FY2025; company-wide constant-currency ARR growth was ~5% in H1 FY2026, which is the medium-term run-rate the base case decelerates from after the guided FY2026 year.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-17.5% 3yr, -7.4% 5yr) and diverges by far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs. This is not a business signal: the company pays out ~70% of net income as dividends plus buybacks and paid a JPY 96bn special dividend and JPY 40bn of buybacks in FY2024 under an explicit no-retained-earnings policy. Book value is not usable as the growth anchor for this name; revenue and constant-currency ARR are.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2020 41,055 -> FY2022 32,802 -> FY2025 36,843. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (4.0%) is below the reported-FCF CAGR (5.2%) because interest income on the cash pile grew from 2,142 to 3,527 over the period; SBC itself is small (0.4-0.5% of revenue) and not a growing share of the economics. Over FY2020-FY2025 owner FCF fell slightly while revenue compounded at 9.7%: the deferred-revenue tailwind in OCF was offset by rising capex (capitalised software and data-centre equipment, 8-11% of revenue) and cash tax, so FCF conversion has not kept pace with reported growth.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 is the maintained FY2026 sales guidance (+9.2%, H1 ran +11.0% with FX help at USD156/EUR183). Thereafter the path steps down to the ~5% constant-currency ARR run-rate and decays to 2% JPY terminal growth; management's 8-10% FY2028 sales CAGR target is treated as the bull case, not the base, because H1 FY2026 ARR grew only ~5% and reaching the target needs the growth pace to roughly double.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin. FY2026 24.2% reproduces the revised JPY 44.4bn operating-income guidance (24.2% - 0.5% SBC - 9.0% D&A = 14.7% operating margin on JPY 301.4bn), down from 31.2% in FY2025, as AI-token and cloud costs plus brand-promotion spend run above plan. Recovery is partial and gradual: operating margin 16.5% FY2027, 18% FY2028, 19% FY2029, 20% from FY2030, i.e. back to the FY2025 level and the 10-year average (~19%), not to management's 25-27% FY2028 target. D&A declines from 9.0% to 8.0% to converge with capex at 8.0% (FY2025 8.3%, H1 FY2026 8.0%), so the terminal-year D&A tax shield does not exceed reinvestment.
base.tax_rationale: 33% cash tax on EBIT: FY2025 cash taxes paid 18,922 on EBIT 57,777 (32.7%); current tax provision 17,686 on pre-tax 52,331 (33.8%). No carryforwards or one-off credits to ramp from.
base.wc_rationale: 10% of the YoY revenue increase. Deferred revenue (85% of revenue) grows with bookings, but receivables and tax timing offset most of it: over FY2021-FY2025 OCF less net income, D&A and SBC netted to roughly zero despite deferred revenue rising ~JPY 97bn, and it fell JPY 9.5bn in H1 FY2026. A small positive capture is the honest residual.

bull.growth_rationale: Management's 8-10% sales CAGR to FY2028 is delivered at the low end as the Vision One credit-based consumption model re-accelerates total ARR into double digits once the legacy standalone-SaaS run-off is lapped; growth then decays to 2.5% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: AI-token costs are passed through via consumption pricing and platform scale; operating margin recovers to 18.2% FY2027, 20.9% FY2028 and 24.0% from FY2029 (32.5% pre-SBC EBITDA - 0.5% - 8.0%), the low end of management's 25-27% FY2028 target, reached a year late.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 sales land slightly under guidance on a firmer yen in H2 (8.5%); thereafter reported growth is ~2%: constant-currency ARR stalls as the legacy run-off matches Vision One gains and platform-consolidation leaders take the enterprise wallet, with a stronger yen eroding the translated USD/EUR book.
bear.margin_rationale: AI-token costs prove structural (table-stakes functionality that cannot be priced through); FY2026 operating margin 14.0% (23.5% - 0.5% - 9.0%, a modest miss of the revised guidance as the virtual-stock-option provision rebuilds with the share price) and only 16.5% at maturity (25.0% - 0.5% - 8.0%), the FY2022-FY2024 range. Capex held at 8.5% as more inference is brought in-house.

scenario_narratives.base: Trend Micro's two axes are (1) whether the AI/cloud-token cost overrun that cut FY2026 operating-income guidance from JPY 56.4bn to 44.4bn is a one-year investment spike or a structural shift in the cost of competing, and (2) whether Vision One/TrendAI (+49% ARR, ~45% of enterprise ARR) can lift company-wide ARR growth off ~5% once the legacy standalone-SaaS run-off is lapped. The base case takes FY2026 at the revised guidance, lets operating margin recover only to ~20% (the FY2025 level and the ten-year average) by FY2030 rather than management's 25-27% FY2028 target, and grows revenue at ~5% constant-currency decaying to 2% in yen. Capex stays at 8% of revenue (capitalised software and data-centre equipment are real reinvestment for this company, which is why FY2025 owner FCF was only 13% of revenue against a 21% operating margin). The result is a steady, cash-generative, net-cash Japanese software franchise growing modestly, valued on the flows it actually produces, with the JPY 226bn of cash and securities added once and the interest on it stripped from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-token cost is a transitional investment that consumption pricing passes through, and the credit-based Vision One model pulls total ARR into double digits as management targets, so sales compound 8-10% to FY2028 and operating margin reaches 24% by FY2029 (the low end of the 25-27% target, a year late). Renewed take-private interest (Bain, Advent, EQT, KKR circled in 2024-25) is not modelled as a premium; it is a reason the bull outcome can be crystallised rather than a separate value.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI functionality becomes table stakes whose inference cost the company bears without pricing power against Microsoft, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks; operating margin settles at 15-16.5% (the FY2022-FY2024 range) and total ARR stalls as legacy run-off cancels platform gains while a firmer yen shrinks the translated USD/EUR book. Growth of ~2% in yen, capex at 8.5% and 1.5% terminal growth. The balance sheet holds (no debt, JPY 226bn cash and securities) so this is a value-trap path, not a solvency one; the ~70% payout plus buybacks continues but on a lower earnings base.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. The thesis rests on an unproven recovery from a cost shock management did not foresee in February and only quantified in August, and H1 FY2026 ARR growth (~5%) is tracking well below the pace the bull case needs; the bull case requires three independent things (cost pass-through, ARR re-acceleration, yen stability) to go right. The bear case is a margin and growth stall, not a solvency event, which is why it is not weighted higher still.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the owner cash flows of a mature, net-cash, J-GAAP security-software company in yen at a yen cost of equity, taking the August 2026 guidance cut at face value for the current year and allowing only a partial, gradual margin recovery thereafter. SBC is expensed and the diluted count held flat; interest income is stripped and the cash plus securities added once in the bridge; capex is kept at the company's actual 8% reinvestment rate rather than a software-peer 2-3%. The house basis is the headline; the street basis differs by only the ~0.5%-of-revenue SBC charge, so the house/street band is narrow for this name.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI-token and cloud cost intensity proves structural, so the base-case recovery to a 20% operating margin by FY2030 does not occur (bear path: 15-16.5%).
Company-wide ARR growth stays at ~5% or lower as legacy standalone-SaaS run-off continues to cancel Vision One gains, undermining even the base-case ~5% growth path.

Yen appreciation: roughly two-thirds of revenue is non-yen; management's FY2026 forecast assumes USD 156 / EUR 183, and a stronger yen cuts reported sales and margins (people cost is partly yen-denominated).
The virtual-stock-option (cash-settled) provision is marked to the share price; the H1 FY2026 cost base was flattered by its release and reverses with the share price near its 52-week high.
Terminal value is roughly 55-60% of enterprise value in the base case; a 1pp change in WACC or terminal growth moves the per-share value materially (see sensitivity grid).
Take-private speculation can hold the price above the fundamental range for extended periods and then unwind; no takeover premium is included in any scenario.
